p.title: The water cycle
p.challenge: Order the water cycle — start with the Sun heating the sea. Where does it start again?
panels: The Sun heats water in seas, rivers and lakes
Evaporation: water turns into vapour and rises
Condensation: vapour cools into droplets — clouds
Precipitation: heavy drops fall as rain, snow or hail
Rain flows to rivers and seas; some soaks into the ground

p.title: Earth's surface in 4 equal parts
p.challenge: Water covers about three-fourths of the Earth's surface. Make the pie show it: 3 parts water, 1 part land

p.title: Rainwater harvesting
p.challenge: Follow the rain from the rooftop. At the question, choose: store it, or send it into the ground?

nodes.info: Without harvesting, this rainwater just flows away and is wasted.
Pipes collect the water from the whole roof.

nodes.text: A filter cleans out leaves and dirt
nodes.info: Sand and gravel keep dirt out of the stored water.
Rainwater harvesting means storing rainwater, or sending it into the ground.

nodes.text: Store it in a tank or kund
nodes.info: In the desert of Rajasthan, covered pits called kunds or tankas store rainwater.
The water soaks in and fills up the groundwater for wells.

p.title: Journey of a river
p.challenge: Put the river's journey in order — from its source to its mouth
panels: Source: it begins at a glacier high in the mountains
In the mountains it is narrow and fast, rolling rocks
Tributaries join it; two rivers meet at a confluence
In the plains it is wide and slow and spreads rich silt
Near the sea it splits into branches and forms a delta
Mouth: the river meets the sea

jobs.mouth: Teeth cut and chew food. The tongue mixes it with saliva, which makes it soft and wet.
jobs.oesophagus: The food pipe carries food from the mouth to the stomach.
jobs.stomach: Digestive juices mix with the food and churn it.
jobs.smallint: Digestion is completed. Useful parts of food go into the blood and reach the whole body.
jobs.largeint: Takes back water from what is left. The waste then leaves the body.

p.title: Safe and healthy eating
p.challenge: Play the steps before a meal. At the question, choose what to do with the food

nodes.info: Washing removes germs that could make us ill.
Washing removes dirt and germs.

nodes.text: Is the food fresh, not mouldy or spoilt?
nodes.info: Keep food covered and cool so it stays safe from flies and dust.
Roti, dal, sabzi and salad: a balanced diet has all nutrients in the right amounts.
Mould can spread inside food, so mouldy food should be thrown away.

p.title: When I feel upset
p.challenge: Play it through: choose Yes or No at each question to find a kind and safe next step

nodes.text: I feel upset, angry or scared
nodes.info: All feelings are okay. Talking about them helps.

nodes.text: Take deep breaths and count to ten
nodes.info: Slow breathing calms the body and mind.

nodes.text: Is someone hurting me again and again?
nodes.info: Bullying means hurting someone again and again with words or actions.
Bullying is never okay. A trusted adult can help stop it.

nodes.text: Talk to a friend or parent
nodes.info: Sharing a feeling makes it lighter.

nodes.text: Be kind: share, listen, include others
nodes.info: Being kind means sharing, helping, listening and including others in games.

HOLD ON until the shaking stops

stories.title: Fire drill
panels: Hear the alarm and stop work
Stay calm and line up
Walk quickly down the stairs, never the lift
Reach the safe open ground
The teacher counts everyone

stories.title: Crossing the road

Look right
Look left
Look right again
Cross when the road is clear

nodes.text: Does the place get very little rain?

Places with plenty of rain are not deserts.
Height makes a place very cold.
Leh is here. Two-humped camels live in the Nubra Valley.
In winter the salt shines white like snow.
A huge salt desert in Gujarat.
Sand dunes, very hot days and cool nights. Jaisalmer is a city in the Thar.

nodes.info: Biogas is made from cow dung and kitchen waste.

nodes.text: Put them in a closed tank with water
nodes.info: The tank is called a biogas plant.

nodes.text: The waste slowly rots in the tank
nodes.info: Tiny living things break down the waste.
Biogas is a renewable source: we can keep making it.

nodes.text: A pipe takes the gas to the stove
nodes.info: Families cook with it. The leftover slurry is good manure.

p.title: Where does this fibre come from?
p.challenge: Pick a fibre in your mind (cotton, jute, wool, silk, nylon…). Answer the questions to find where it comes from

nodes.text: Is it made in a factory from chemicals?
nodes.info: Synthetic fibres are made from chemicals that come from petroleum.
Man-made in factories.

nodes.text: Does it come from a plant?
nodes.info: Plant fibres come from bolls, stems or husks.
Cotton from bolls, jute from the stem, coir from coconut husks. Cotton keeps us cool.
Wool from the hair of sheep, goats, yaks and camels; silk from silkworm cocoons. Wool keeps us warm.

nodes.info: Separate waste at home: wet and dry go in different bins.

nodes.text: Wet waste, like peels or food?
nodes.info: Wet waste comes from food and plants.
Green bin = wet waste.
Compost is a natural manure.
Paper, plastic, metal and glass are dry waste.
The 3 Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.

p.title: Why is the Earth getting warmer?
p.challenge: Put the causes and effects in order: from burning fuel to melting glaciers — and the fix!
panels: We burn coal, petrol and diesel and cut down forests
More carbon dioxide goes into the air
This gas traps heat, so the Earth slowly gets warmer
Glaciers melt and sea levels rise
More heatwaves, very heavy rain or long dry spells
We help: plant trees, save electricity, walk or cycle
